answer_text:
Let

\[
P(x)=x^{20}-7x^3+1
\]

with roots \(r_1,\dots,r_{20}\). Since

\[
P(i)=2+7i\neq 0,\qquad P(-i)=2-7i\neq 0,
\]

none of the roots is \(\pm i\), so the desired sum is well-defined.

Use the partial fraction decomposition

\[
\frac{1}{r^2+1}
=\frac{1}{(r-i)(r+i)}
=\frac{1}{2i}\left(\frac{1}{r-i}-\frac{1}{r+i}\right).
\]

Thus

\[
S=\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{r_k^2+1}
=\frac{1}{2i}\left(\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{r_k-i}
-\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{r_k+i}\right).
\]

For a monic polynomial \(P(x)=\prod_{k=1}^{20}(x-r_k)\),

\[
\frac{P'(a)}{P(a)}=\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{a-r_k}.
\]

Therefore,

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{r_k-i}
=-\frac{P'(i)}{P(i)}
\]

and

\[
\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{r_k+i}
=\sum_{k=1}^{20}\frac{1}{r_k-(-i)}
=-\frac{P'(-i)}{P(-i)}.
\]

So

\[
S=\frac{1}{2i}\left(-\frac{P'(i)}{P(i)}+\frac{P'(-i)}{P(-i)}\right).
\]

Now compute the needed values. Since

\[
P'(x)=20x^{19}-21x^2,
\]

we have

\[
P(i)=i^{20}-7i^3+1=1+7i+1=2+7i,
\]

\[
P'(i)=20i^{19}-21i^2=20(-i)+21=21-20i,
\]

\[
P(-i)=(-i)^{20}-7(-i)^3+1=1-7i+1=2-7i,
\]

\[
P'(-i)=20(-i)^{19}-21(-i)^2=20i+21=21+20i.
\]

Hence

\[
S=\frac{1}{2i}\left(
-\frac{21-20i}{2+7i}
+\frac{21+20i}{2-7i}
\right).
\]

The second fraction is the complex conjugate of the first. Let

\[
A=\frac{21-20i}{2+7i}.
\]

Then

\[
A=\frac{(21-20i)(2-7i)}{2^2+7^2}
=\frac{42-147i-40i-140}{53}
=\frac{-98-187i}{53}.
\]

Thus

\[
S=\frac{1}{2i}(-A+\overline{A})
=-\operatorname{Im}(A)
=\frac{187}{53}.
\]

So \(m=187\) and \(n=53\), giving

\[
m+n=187+53=240.
\]

\[
\boxed{240}
\]
